title: Christian Education, Character, and Wisdom
author: Simon P. Kennedy
summary: Dr. Simon P. Kennedy argues in this lecture adaptation that character should be the centerpiece of Christian education and that the best route to it is wisdom, pursued through a liberal arts or classical approach. He defines education as the deliberate formation of a person and roots the idea in the Greek paideia, which Plato describes as turning the soul toward the true, the good and the beautiful. He traces how the early church took up paideia as Christian formation, so that Christian education and classical education become, in his words, the same tradition. Drawing on Aristotle, Charlotte Mason and James Arthur, he says the aim of education is not knowledge, taste or manners but good character, which is the settled disposition behind virtuous action. Because wise people choose the good, wisdom is the foundation of character, and he supports the point with 2 Peter 1 and Proverbs 1. Character education and Christian education therefore belong together.
points: Education is defined as the deliberate formation of a person toward an aim, which ties it to the Greek idea of paideia and a purpose beyond information transfer.
Christian education descends from the early church's adoption of paideia, which is why the author calls it classical education.
The stated aim of education is character, not knowledge, aesthetic sensitivity or good manners.
Everyone has a character but not everyone is virtuous, so virtues are the parts of character that education must deliberately train.
Wisdom undergirds character, so growing in wisdom, beginning with the fear of the Lord, is the process that makes character formation possible.
quotes: My working definition of education is “the deliberate formation of a person.

Plato uses the word paideia to describe what we call education. In his Republic, Plato says that paideia refers to the process of a person being turned towards the true, the good, and the beautiful. This means that education is not just downloading information or simply increasing in knowledge.

Education is a training, but it is training for the soul rather than the body. It is the deliberate formation of a person through discipline, training, and instruction, where the person is directed towards the true, the good, and the beautiful.
From this came a tradition of Christian education we now call “classical.” Understood this way, Christian education is classical education.

The aim of education is not knowledge, aesthetic sensitivity, good manners, or good taste. The aim is character. The aim is to form students of good character, to train, disciple, and form good people.
Everyone has a character, but not everyone is virtuous. Your character is whatever you are, and what you are can be made up of virtuous characteristics or vicious ones.

Without wisdom, you cannot have good character, which is the main point of Christian education. It is wisdom that undergirds the desire for, and ability to choose, the true, the good, and the beautiful.
